title: Explicit differential comparison for simultaneous outer scalar extension
statement: Let $A_0,B_0,C_0,T$ be commutative rings, with $B_0,C_0,T$ $A_0$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ an $A_0$-algebra map. Put $B_T=T\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_T=T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, and give $C_T$ its $B_T$-algebra structure by $t\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes\varphi_0(b)$. Write $M_0=\Omega_{C_0/B_0}$ for the module of Kähler differentials with universal derivation $\mathrm d_0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and write $\mathrm d_T$ for the universal $B_T$-derivation of $C_T$. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The formulas $q_T((t\otimes b)\otimes c)=t\otimes\varphi_0(b)c$ and $q_T^{-1}(t\otimes c)=(t\otimes1)\otimes c$ define inverse $B_T$-algebra isomorphisms $B_T\otimes_{B_0}C_0\simeq C_T$. There are inverse $C_T$-linear isomorphisms $h_T:C_T\otimes_{C_0}M_0\simeq T\otimes_{A_0}M_0$ given by $h_T((t\otimes c)\otimes\omega)=t\otimes c\omega$ and $h_T^{-1}(t\otimes\omega)=(t\otimes1)\otimes\omega$, where $(t\otimes c)\cdot(u\otimes\omega)=tu\otimes c\omega$ is the $C_T$-action on the right. Finally the canonical differential base-change map for $B_0\to B_T$ and $B_0\to C_0$, transported by $q_T$ and $h_T$, is a $C_T$-linear isomorphism $F_T:T\otimes_{A_0}M_0\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{C_T/B_T}$ with $F_T(t\otimes\mathrm d_0c)=(t\otimes1)\,\mathrm d_T(1\otimes c)$ for all $t\in T,c\in C_0$. No finite-generation or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the tensor universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The proposed $q_T$ is additive in each entry and balanced: for $a\in A_0$, $ta\otimes\varphi_0(b)c=t\otimes\varphi_0(ab)c$, and for $b'\in B_0$, $t\otimes\varphi_0(bb')c=t\otimes\varphi_0(b)\varphi_0(b')c$. The proposed inverse is $A_0$-balanced because $(ta\otimes1)\otimes c=(t\otimes a)\otimes c=(t\otimes1)\otimes ac$. The rings $B_T$, $C_T$ and $B_T\otimes_{B_0}C_0$ carry the multiplication $(x\otimes y)(x'\otimes y')=xx'\otimes yy'$ with unit $1\otimes1$ of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1), and $B_T\to C_T$, $t\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes\varphi_0(b)$, is the ring map given by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](2) for $T\to C_T$, $t\mapsto t\otimes1$, and $B_0\to C_T$, $b\mapsto1\otimes\varphi_0(b)$. Both proposed maps preserve products of pure tensors and units by this rule, hence, being additive, preserve all products. Their composites on generators are $t\otimes c\mapsto t\otimes c$ and $(t\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes\varphi_0(b)c=(t\otimes b)\otimes c$. The forward map sends $(t\otimes b)\otimes1$ to $t\otimes\varphi_0(b)$, the specified $B_T$-structure on $C_T$; hence both are $B_T$-algebra maps. Additivity extends these identities to all tensors.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), balancing relations; Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), scalar-extended rings

proof.text: By the same tensor universal property, $h_T$ is well defined: its $A_0$-balancing is $ta\otimes c\omega=t\otimes ac\omega$, and its $C_0$-balancing is $t\otimes(cc')\omega=t\otimes c(c'\omega)$. The inverse is $A_0$-balanced since $(ta\otimes1)\otimes\omega=(t\otimes a)\otimes\omega=(t\otimes1)\otimes a\omega$. The action $(t\otimes c)(u\otimes\omega)=tu\otimes c\omega$ respects the tensor relations; multiplication, unit and distributivity follow on pure tensors and extend by additivity. The inverse composites are $t\otimes\omega\mapsto t\otimes\omega$ and $(t\otimes c)\otimes\omega\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes c\omega=(t\otimes c)\otimes\omega$. Finally, for $u,t\in T$ and $c',c\in C_0$, both $h_T(((u\otimes c')(t\otimes c))\otimes\omega)$ and $(u\otimes c')h_T((t\otimes c)\otimes\omega)$ equal $ut\otimes c'c\omega$. Thus $h_T$ and its inverse are $C_T$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), explicit balancing and inverse calculations

proof.text: Put $D=B_T\otimes_{B_0}C_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] with $R=B_0$, $R'=B_T$, $S=C_0$, $S'=D$. Its hypotheses are just the given ring maps; it supplies the canonical isomorphism $B_T\otimes_{B_0}M_0\to\Omega_{D/B_T}$, sending $b_T\otimes\mathrm d_0c$ to $b_T\,\mathrm d_D(1\otimes c)$, and its $D$-linear form $D\otimes_{C_0}M_0\simeq\Omega_{D/B_T}$. Explicitly the two domains are identified by $(b_T\otimes c)\otimes\omega\mapsto b_T\otimes c\omega$, with inverse $b_T\otimes\omega\mapsto(b_T\otimes1)\otimes\omega$; balancing and the inverse identities are the calculations of step 2. To transport differentials along $q_T$, the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] applied to $\mathrm d_T\circ q_T$ gives $\mathrm d_D z\mapsto\mathrm d_T(q_Tz)$; applying it to $q_T^{-1}$ gives its inverse. Their composites fix every differential generator, hence are identities. The ring $D$ has the multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1). Since $q_T(1\otimes c)=1\otimes c$, $q_T$ is $C_0$-linear for $c\mapsto(1\otimes1)\otimes c$ and $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, so $q_T^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{M_0}:C_T\otimes_{C_0}M_0\to D\otimes_{C_0}M_0$ is defined by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], is inverse to $q_T\otimes\mathrm{id}_{M_0}$ by compatibility with composition and identities, and is $C_T$-linear when $C_T$ acts on the target through $q_T^{-1}$. Let $\beta$ be the composite of $q_T^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{M_0}$, the domain identification above, the canonical isomorphism, and the differential transport. Consequently this transported canonical map is a $C_T$-linear isomorphism $\beta:C_T\otimes_{C_0}M_0\simeq\Omega_{C_T/B_T}$ and $\beta(1\otimes\mathrm d_0c)=\mathrm d_T(1\otimes c)$, since $q_T(1\otimes c)=1\otimes c$. This uses only the cited theorem and the universal property, with no finiteness or flatness.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), canonical isomorphism and its universal-derivation formula; Tags 07BK (definition-differentials) and 00RO (lemma-universal-omega)

proof.text: Define $F_T=\beta\circ h_T^{-1}$. Both factors are $C_T$-linear isomorphisms, so this is precisely the canonical base-change isomorphism transported by $q_T$ and $h_T$. For $t\in T$ and $c\in C_0$, $h_T^{-1}(t\otimes\mathrm d_0c)=(t\otimes1)\otimes\mathrm d_0c=(t\otimes1)\cdot(1\otimes\mathrm d_0c)$; applying the $C_T$-linear map $\beta$ and its formula from step 3 gives $F_T(t\otimes\mathrm d_0c)=(t\otimes1)\,\mathrm d_T(1\otimes c)$. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves every clause.
